chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Yahya ibn al-Mubarik, from Abdullah ibn Jabala, from Abu Jamilyah, from Isḥaq ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said to Shurayh: 'O Shurayh, you have taken a seat that no one occupies except a Prophet, or the Prophet's successor, or a fortunate one.'

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (title for Imam Ali)
key_terms.الشَّقِيّ: The fortunate one (one who attains success/salvation)
key_terms.الْوَصِيُّ: The successor (specifically referring to the Imams)
key_terms.شُرَيْح: Shurayh ibn al-Harith, a famous early Islamic judge

ai.seo_question: What does Imam Ali say about the status of a judge in relation to Prophets and Imams?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) elevates the station of the judge Shurayh, asserting that the authority to adjudicate is a divine trust reserved for Prophets, their infallible successors (Imams), or the divinely fortunate. This classification underscores the Shia view of judicial power not merely as a legal function but as a spiritual hierarchy, linking earthly justice to prophetic legacy and divine favor.
